findings.highlight: I've been telling the others about these things
findings.evidenceJa: わたしがあることないこと発信してるからこそ、みんながあなたに親しみ持ってくれてるんだけどなぁ。
findings.explanation: Nakagawa cheerfully admits to spreading both true and made-up stories about Koharu, claiming that this rumor mill is why the staff feel close to her. The English reduces this to telling them unspecified 'things,' deleting the self-incriminating comic characterization and the actual means by which familiarity was manufactured.
findings.japanese:
「わたしがあることないこと発信してるからこそ、
みんながあなたに親しみ持ってくれてるんだけどなぁ。
ちょっとは感謝してくれたって…」
findings.todokanai: "It's because I've been telling the others about these things that everyone's able to feel familiar with you. You could at least be a little grateful for that…"

findings.highlight: I don't plan to get along with everyone in my workplace
findings.evidenceJa: わたしは別に仕事で馴れ合いするつもりないですから
findings.explanation: Koharu says she has no intention of turning work into cozy social fraternization or an in-group clique. The English makes her say she does not intend to get along with anyone, changing a rigidly professional stance into broad antisocial hostility that the surrounding staff relationships contradict.
findings.japanese: 「わたしは別に仕事で馴れ合いするつもりないですから」
findings.todokanai: "I don't plan to get along with everyone in my workplace."

findings.highlight: pitying someone is also a form of affection
findings.evidenceJa: 人としての尊敬だって愛だけどね？憐れみだって恋だけどね？
findings.explanation: Nakagawa traps Koharu by insisting first that respect is 愛 and then, more provocatively, that pity is 恋—the specifically romantic word Koharu is trying to disavow. Rendering the second term as generic affection removes the escalation into romantic feeling and weakens the reason Koharu immediately retreats.
findings.japanese:
「人としての尊敬だって愛だけどね？
憐れみだって恋だけどね？」
findings.todokanai: "Respecting someone as a person is also a form of love, right? And pitying someone is also a form of affection, is it not?"

findings.highlight: If Senpai wants to talk about it, I'll be there
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩が言いたくなったら話してくれるはずです。それも約束しましたから
findings.explanation: Koharu says that when Haruki wants to speak, he is supposed to tell her, and that this too was part of their promise. The English substitutes the generic assurance that she will be there, erasing Haruki's promised future act of confiding in her—the new intimacy that alarms Takeya.
findings.japanese:
「先輩が言いたくなったら話してくれるはずです。
それも約束しましたから」
findings.todokanai: "If Senpai wants to talk about it, I'll be there. That's the promise we made."
